Kids 6 · Checkpoint 5
Final presentation · 3 + 5 + 2 = 10 points
Learning Well 6 · Units 1 to 9

Pick Your
Project

Three projects, same six moves, same ten points. Open a folder to read what each one asks for, see Theo’s poster, and read the plan he wrote before presenting.

Três projetos, os mesmos seis movimentos, os mesmos dez pontos. Abra uma pasta para ver o que cada projeto pede e como o Theo planejou o dele.

Step 1 · Choose your track

Click a folder. Clique numa pasta.

Step 2 · The plan · this is where the work is

Notes, not a text

Everybody writes their plan before presenting. But a plan is not the speech written down. If you write full sentences, you will read them out loud on the day, and reading is not presenting.

Write the smallest thing that reminds you what to say. Then build the sentence with your mouth, in front of us.

Pages 2 and 3 of the notebook show Theo’s own plan, in all three tracks. Copy the shape of it, not the content.

Not this

In my project I used the idea of the beaver because beavers build dams and my invention is a wall that stops the water in my street when it rains a lot.

This

Beaver → dam → wall for street water
why: cheap, sustainable
my brother built the model

Hand in One week before your presentation. No plan, no presentation that day.

O plano é entregue uma semana antes e volta corrigido. Sem plano entregue, a apresentação fica para outro dia. Escreva em tópicos, não em frases: quem escreve frase lê no dia, e ler não é apresentar.

Step 3 · The consulting round

In class, after your plan comes back, you have fifteen minutes to walk around and ask three classmates and your teacher one question: what would you change in my project?

Write their answers in English while they are talking, in your notebook. You will need those words in Move 5, and you cannot invent them.

Na aula, depois que o plano volta corrigido, você tem quinze minutos para circular e perguntar a três colegas e à professora o que eles mudariam no seu projeto. Anote em inglês na hora.

Step 4 · The six moves

1

Where the idea came from

Say how long the subject has been in your life, and when you decided to do this.

Design Fair
I've been interested in animals since I was seven. I found the beaver on a website in April.
Behind the Scenes
We've watched a lot of films this year. We decided to make our own in May.
Exchange Club
I've never been to Canada before. My cousin lived in Toronto for two years.
2

How it was before

Say how people did this in the past, and what is different now.

Design Fair
People used to build walls with concrete. They didn't use to copy animals.
Behind the Scenes
Films didn't use to have sound. Actors used to wear heavy make-up.
Exchange Club
My host school used to be a farm. Students didn't use to wear a uniform.
3

Who did what

Say who made the parts, what had already happened before you started, and what has been going on since.

Design Fair
The model was built by my brother. Scientists had already studied beavers when I started.
Behind the Scenes
The music was recorded by Ana. We had already written the script when we found a camera.
Exchange Club
The tower was built in 1976. Tourists have been climbing it ever since.
4

What it is

Show what you brought and describe it with the words of your units. Say why it is good, not only what it is.

Design Fair
The structure is simple and reliable. It's sustainable, user-friendly and cheap to repair.
Behind the Scenes
The set was small, but the atmosphere was great. The costumes were stylish and the make-up was terrible.
Exchange Club
The city is bright and freezing. The food was sweet and a bit strange.
5

The voices

Bring in the people from Step 3. Say what they said, what they told you to do, and what they asked you.

Design Fair
A classmate told me to make it smaller. My teacher asked me if I had measured it.
Behind the Scenes
Ana said that the ending was confusing. She told me not to forget the credits.
Exchange Club
My host mother told me to try the maple syrup. A student asked me if people spoke English at home.
6

With no limits

Finish with the version you could not do this year. Money, time and space are not a problem now.

Design Fair
If I had a 3D printer, I would build it for real.
Behind the Scenes
If we had a drone, we would film the whole school from above.
Exchange Club
If I had one more month, I would learn to skate properly.

Before the day · rehearsing

O Theo se filmou em casa para ouvir o próprio inglês antes do dia. Isso é ensaio e ajuda muito. O vídeo não é a entrega: no dia você fala ao vivo, olhando para as suas anotações.

And then: two questions

When you finish, your teacher asks you two questions about your project. You will not know them before. Answer in full sentences, in English.

Ao terminar, a professora faz duas perguntas sobre o seu projeto. Você não recebe essas perguntas antes. Responda em frases completas, em inglês.

Step 5 · And then you write it

The week after you present, turn your notes into a real text of 80 to 100 words, on page 7 of the notebook. Not before: writing it first turns the talk into reading. Writing it after is different, because you already know what worked and what confused people.

Na semana seguinte à apresentação, você transforma as suas anotações num texto de 80 a 100 palavras, na página 7 do caderno. Não antes: escrever antes transforma a fala em leitura.

Two rules

The clip is not the project

On Track B, your video may run for 60 seconds and it replaces nothing. You still speak all six moves yourself.

O vídeo tem 60 segundos e não substitui nenhum movimento. Você fala os seis do mesmo jeito.

Made by you

The model, the poster or the map has to be made by you. It does not have to be beautiful. It has to be yours.

A maquete, o pôster ou o mapa precisa ser feito por você. Não precisa ser bonito, precisa ser seu.

What counts · 10 points

The plan, handed in on paper

Entregue uma semana antes.

  1. Your track, your idea in one line, and your model, poster or map1 pt
  2. The six moves filled in as notes, not as sentences1 pt
  3. The notes from your consulting round, in English1 pt
Subtotal3 points

The presentation

No dia, na frente da turma.

  1. Says where the idea came from and how it was before1 pt
  2. Says who did what, and what had already happened1 pt
  3. Describes it with the words of the units, and shows what you brought1 pt
  4. Brings in what people said, told you to do, or asked you1 pt
  5. Speaks from notes, not from a written text, and answers the two questions1 pt
Subtotal5 points

The write-up

Página 7 do caderno, entregue na semana seguinte à apresentação.

  1. 80 to 100 words, in full sentences1 pt
  2. Keeps three of the six moves in the text1 pt
Subtotal2 points
Total10 points

Erros de pronúncia e pequenos erros de gramática não tiram ponto. Cada linha vale 1 ponto e é marcada como feita ou não feita. No portal, a apresentação entra em campo separado: a prova escrita vale 40 pontos e a apresentação vale estes 10.

Take your notebook home

The notebook has seven pages: your track, Theo’s own plan in all three tracks, the six moves in note form, the consulting round, your drawing, and the write-up you hand in after presenting.
